top_choice_rationale: P001 (Autor, Hanson and Dorn, cited for empirical analyses of how import competition and technological change reshape labour demand, local labour markets and wage inequality) addresses a first-order question with transparent designs and open data. The work has been replicated, re-analysed and contested for about a decade. The disputes concern the size and persistence of the effects, not whether adjustment is slow and costly, so the core finding has survived hostile scrutiny. Autor, Dorn and Hanson jointly wrote the central China-shock papers, so credit is clean if the citation stays empirical and does not claim the task-model theory whose originators lie outside the credited set. P002 (Melitz and Helpman) is more mature and has a tight two-name credit, but I rank it second. I find the two close on common criteria. My preference rests on the scrutiny record and explanatory reach, not on a decisive scientific gap. Both are far preferable to no award.
